Son Sold Dad's 1972 Pontiac Luxury LeMans After Many Years in Hiding, Restoration Now Needed
44 photos
Photo: eBay seller spoilerecw
Two owners. Oklahoma car. Original engine and transmission. Parked for years before the owner’s son decided to let it go. These are the main things you must have in mind when checking out this 1972 Pontiac Luxury LeMans.
This Pontiac landed on eBay in project car condition, so what it needs today is a restoration. This would be the first major refresh in its life, and despite the seller advertising a car that has never been “modified or tampered with,” you’ll discover that it has already received some changes.
For example, the driver’s fender has already been replaced (though the original rusty one is still available), while the grille comes from a 1971 T-37 (with two correct sets also being offered).
That is why I recommend that any restoration guy who thinks he can save this Luxury LeMans calls the seller and arranges an in-person inspection. This unrestored and unaltered promise sounds almost too good to be true, so you must see everything with your own eyes before making an offer.
Photo: eBay seller spoilerecw The Luxury LeMans wasn’t as popular as the GTO , but in 1972, it was certainly the model that brought home more bacon. Sales of the GTO were already going down after the decline started earlier in the same decade, so this model ended the year with only a little over 5,800 cars sold to American buyers.
The Luxury LeMans didn’t suffer from the exclusive performance-oriented DNA as the GTO, so it managed to convince over 46,000 buyers in 1972.
The base engine on the Luxury LeMans was a 350 rated at 160 horsepower (this was the net rating that came into effect this year). Pontiac also offered several big-block upgrades, including a 455, without giving buyers the option to order the 455-4 with a Rochester four-barrel carburetor and 250 horsepower. This engine was available on all LeMans configurations, except for the Luxury.
As for what made the Luxury LeMans luxurious, it was the focus on comfort rather than on performance. Each car was fitted with plush carpets, a padded steering wheel, and standard fender skirts. Pontiac also offered a special instrument panel, as well as a special grille, trim, and badging to make it obvious that you drove a Luxury LeMans.
This model survived in the following years, eventually evolving into the Grand LeMans when the 1975 model year came out.
Photo: eBay seller spoilerecw This 1972 Luxury LeMans has already been refreshed mechanically. It’s fitted with the base Pontiac 350 two-barrel engine paired with an automatic transmission. The carburetor was rebuilt, and the car has new brakes, new hoses, a new alternator, and so on. The gas tank has also been cleaned, but the gas gauge doesn’t work.
Otherwise, the car is in running shape, so if you want to hop in and take it for a spin, you should be able to do this during your in-person inspection.
But any diehard Pontiac guy will want to deal with the obvious problems first. There’s obvious rust on this LeMans, though I think the existing damage isn’t by any means critical. It’s just typical corrosion that a good metal guy will deal with quite easily, but that’s why I recommended that you see the car in person.
If you raise it on a lift, determining how many repairs it needs is much easier.
The windshield is also cracked, and the culprit is a tree limb that fell on the car during a storm a few years ago. Otherwise, it’s a solid restoration candidate that can also become a father-son project for the winter.
Photo: eBay seller spoilerecw Let’s be honest here. A 1972 Pontiac Luxury LeMans isn’t necessarily the most desirable car, and that’s why such a project must be priced accordingly to let it find a new home fast.
GTOs and big-block LeMans projects continue to be icing on the cake for the 1972 model year, so despite being quite a special car, a Luxury LeMans is hardly a collectible. A diehard Pontiac fanboy would obviously love to own such a car, but otherwise, it’s hard to believe that anyone would pay big bucks for such a car.
Fortunately, the seller looks realistic, so the auction they started on eBay begins at $5,000. Nobody has entered the digital fight so far, but considering a reserve is also in place, this could be why. Potential buyers might be afraid that the reserve is unrealistic, so if you want this car, you should just call the seller and ask all your questions on this front.
The auction ends in a little over 5 days, so theoretically, you have all the time in the world to arrange an in-person inspection and also go there to figure out what this car needs. The vehicle is parked in Eakly, Oklahoma, and despite its running condition, taking it home on a trailer is probably the recommended approach, considering it’s still a project.
Via // eBay
